Get started with zuroar

zuroar.Rmd

zuroar gives R compressed sets of whole numbers from 0 to 2^32 - 1, or to 2^64 - 1 with the 64-bit class. Dense stretches and long runs take a fraction of the memory of a plain vector, and membership, counts and set operations work without expanding them. Bitmaps are written in the portable Roaring format that Python, Java, Go and Rust programs share.

library(zuroar)

Build a bitmap

roar() takes whole numbers in any order, with or without duplicates. roar_range() takes both ends of a range, included as in seq(), and roar_add() and roar_remove() return a changed copy.

x <- roar(c(1L, 5L, 9L, 100000L))
x <- roar_add(x, 7L)
x <- roar_remove(x, 5L)
y <- roar_range(1, 1e6)
y <- roar_remove(y, from = 10, to = 19)

Use it like a sorted vector

A bitmap behaves like sort(unique(v)): length() counts its values, positions start at 1, [ returns a bitmap and [[ a single value. c() is the union, and adding a number shifts every value.

length(x)
#> [1] 4
x[[2]]
#> [1] 7
x[2:3]
head(y, 3)
c(x, roar(42L)) + 10

Ask questions

roar_contains() is the fast membership test. Ranges are inclusive, roar_rank() counts the values at or below one, roar_select() finds the k-th smallest, and roar_next() the nearest value above.

roar_contains(x, c(5L, 6L))
#> [1] FALSE FALSE
roar_count(y, from = 10, to = 20)
#> [1] 1
roar_rank(x, 9L)
#> [1] 3
roar_select(x, c(1, 2))
#> [1] 1 7
roar_next(x, 8L)
#> [1] 9

Combine sets

Between bitmaps, | is the union, & the intersection and <= a subset test. Counts and similarities need no intermediate bitmap.

x | y
x & y
x <= y
roar_cardinality(x, y, op = "and")
roar_jaccard(x, y)

Save and share

roar_serialize() writes the portable format as a raw vector, and roar_unserialize() checks bytes before reading them. A bitmap doesn’t survive saveRDS() on its own; roar_serial_config() lets it travel to mirai workers.

b <- roar_serialize(x)
x2 <- roar_unserialize(b)
mirai::daemons(2, serial = roar_serial_config())

The reference index documents every function, including the 64-bit class, roar64(). An article with benchmarks against base R and the bit package is planned.
